📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hyundai absolutely knocked the teasers for then Hyundai N Vision 74 out of the park. I mean, a hydrogen-electric hybrid that's an actual sports car, with all the style of a 1970s wedge car? The internet loved the idea. But, unfortunately, that's probably what the N Vision will remain—an idea. The intends for production are on ice.

Industry observers note that simon Loasby, the head of Hyundai's Design Center, explained toThe Drive that the decision came down to business. When the South Korean automaker simply couldn't justify the business case for the car, it decided to not move forward with production in the foreseeable future. Here's what Loasby told the publication when asked if the automaker planned to make a production version of the N Vision 74:.

At the moment, no. We were really on it. We had the production clay model of it and the exterior, interior, and so on.

It comes down to the maths of how you judge what the business case is. And that if you’re very tight with the business case on only that car, the volumes of that car and the impact, you got no chance.

If you open it to the overall brand-raising profile value of that, you have a bigger chance. But as yet, [no].

Many of you reading this are likely part car lover and part EV enthusiast. Me too, which is why I'm immensely disappointed that Hyundai decided to cancel prepares to build this awesome concept.

After all, EVs are damn fun. Instant torque, low center of gravity. It's pretty much everything that an an enthusiast wants out of a sports car—even if EVs inherently are a bit heavier and lack a row-your-own gearbox. It also used the beloved Stinger as a base to build the car. But rather than the 3.3-liter twin-turbocharged V6, Hyundai stuffed it with the Nexo's hydrogen fuel cells and two electric motors.

That said, not all has gone to waste.

Recent findings suggest that one of the coolest parts of the coupe was its retro styling. That was inspired by the original Hyundai Pony coupe, which was designed by the legendary Giorgetto Giugiaro (the same guy who designed the VW Golf, DeLorean DMC-12, and a plethora of other icons).

Loasby says that Hyundai's head of design, SangYup Lee, convinced the tech giant not to throw away the design work from the N Vision concept. Instead, it reused some of the design elements for upcoming models like the all new 2027 Hyundai Elantra.

In a recent development, "[T]hat top view as you notice, even in the pillar and side view up to the roof crease and the flatness of the roof, that’s all playbook N74," he told The Drive. He later hinted more could be coming: “Just imagine what an N version of [Elantra] can be. It’s really good, it’s awesome.”.

In a recent development, maybe it was the idea of using hydrogen that killed the N Vision concept. Or perhaps that coupes have seem to go the way of the dodo in recent years. Whatever the reason, it's just unfortunate for enthusiasts who were pumped to see a sport-tuned FCEV in the distance.

According to recent reports, one glimmer of hope is that Loasby didn't say that the car is dead forever. Just that Hyundai couldn't make a business case for it "at the moment." Perhaps we might get something with two-doors, a striking design, and battery power in the future. Until then, I'm staying pumped about the Rivian R3X.

Scientists discover that the heart doesn't age the way we thought

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1668 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that as the heart gets older, inflammation increases, but scientists have not fully understood where these changes occur or which parts of the organ are most affected.
  • In a study of mouse hearts published in Aging Cell, the researchers discovered that signs of inflammation and tissue scarring were especially concentrated around the aortic valves and aortic root.
  • Recent findings suggest that "Some of the markers associated with inflammaging were there from the very beginning in young hearts, but they were focused specifically in areas no one had defined before, in the valves and the aorta rather than in muscle tissue," noted study author Nadia Rosenthal, scientific director at JAX.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that as the heart gets older, inflammation increases, but scientists have not fully understood where these changes occur or which parts of the organ are most affected. Researchers at The Jackson Laboratory (JAX) have now uncovered a surprising pattern: Certain regions of the heart appear to be hotspots for aging-related inflammation, offering upcoming clues about how the heart changes over time.

In a study of mouse hearts published in Aging Cell, the researchers discovered that signs of inflammation and tissue scarring were especially concentrated around the aortic valves and aortic root. These areas contain immune cells and connective tissue cells whose interactions change with age, potentially affecting the surrounding heart muscle. The findings provide a fresh picture of cardiac aging and could guide future efforts to understand cardiovascular disease.

Recent findings suggest that "Some of the markers associated with inflammaging were there from the very beginning in young hearts, but they were focused specifically in areas no one had defined before, in the valves and the aorta rather than in muscle tissue," noted study author Nadia Rosenthal, scientific director at JAX. "We really have to think of aging as something that is not linear, because just like we know that people don't age at the same rate, what we know now is that organs and tissues don't age at the same rate either, even within one individual.".

Much of the previous research on heart aging has centered on cardiac muscle, particularly the left ventricle. This chamber performs the essential task of pumping blood into the aorta and throughout the body. By studying the heart as a whole, rather than concentrating primarily on its muscle, the JAX team uncovered important changes in other tissues and the ways their cells interact.

"The valves and the major blood vessels are parts often thought of as plumbing rather than the main engine, but this is a very complicated little machine," Rosenthal said. "It turns out they're home to many of the cells we're interested in, and that's where some of the most key aging-related signals were concentrated.".

Mapping Hidden Hotspots of Heart Aging.

Growing older is the single greatest risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet many of the cellular processes responsible for the heart's decline remain poorly understood. One challenge is that mammalian heart muscle cells have very little ability to regenerate or replace themselves. To investigate what happens as the heart ages, Rosenthal and her colleagues used advanced techniques that allowed them to study thousands of individual cells from young and old mice while also identifying their locations within the heart.

Scientists already know that aging is accompanied by a persistent, low level of inflammation throughout the body. Earlier studies have found similar changes in the heart, including an increase in immune cells that regulate inflammatory activity (macrophages) and cells that produce and maintain connective tissue and contribute to scar formation (fibroblasts).

The new analysis indicated that aging macrophages became more active in genes involved in inflammation and changes to tissue structure. Fibroblasts, meanwhile, increasingly displayed molecular characteristics associated with fibrosis (or scarring). Crucially, the researchers went beyond identifying which genes were active. They also mapped the locations of these cells, making it possible to see how different regions of the heart change as they grow older.

Sources indicate that this approach revealed that inflammation and fibrosis (or scarring) were not distributed uniformly. Instead, the strongest signals appeared around the heart valves and aortic root. The researchers believe these regions may act as key centers of cardiac aging, where changes in supporting cells could influence the health of nearby heart muscle.

According to recent reports, "To keep muscle cells happy, the other cells in the heart have to continue supporting them throughout life," Rosenthal said. "What this study does, for the first time, is provide a comprehensive picture of how those support cells, particularly fibroblasts and macrophages, change with age and contribute to what we call inflammaging.".

Surprising Signs of Aging in Young Hearts.

Another unexpected discovery challenged assumptions about how scientists identify aging cells. The team examined molecular markers frequently associated with cellular senescence, a state in which cells permanently lose the ability to divide, often because of aging or stress. As senescent cells accumulate, they can contribute to ongoing inflammation, tissue damage, and diseases associated with older age.

Surprisingly, some of these supposedly age-related markers were already present in young mouse hearts. Their presence suggests that the markers alone cannot reliably establish whether a cell has entered senescence, and that their meaning may depend on where they appear and the condition of the surrounding tissue.

Industry observers note that "What surprised us was that some of these markers that have been associated with aging were already present in young hearts. They weren't where anyone expected to find them, and that forced us to rethink what those markers are telling us," Rosenthal mentioned. "That turns the usual interpretation of cardiac aging on its ear because these markers alone don't mean a cell is senescent. There's nothing senescent about a six-month-old mouse heart.".

Recent findings suggest that the researchers also identified genes that became more active with age and were especially prominent in the same regions. Among them were Ccl8, which helps transmit inflammatory signals, and Cdkn1a (also known as p21), a gene widely used as an indicator of cellular senescence. Their locations provided further evidence that the valves and aortic root may be particularly crucial areas for understanding how the heart ages.

"We're not talking about single genes. We're talking about an entire conversation between immune cells and fibroblasts. As the heart ages, the way those cells communicate changes, and that shift appears to be linked to the inflammation and tissue remodeling we see in older hearts," Rosenthal said.

Male and Female Hearts Show Different Aging Patterns.

The study uncovered another crucial distinction: Aging did not produce exactly the same molecular changes in male and female mouse hearts.

In a recent development, in males, aging fibroblasts indicated stronger connections to biological processes associated with fibrosis. In females, the corresponding changes were more closely related to pathways involved in heart development and protein production.

In a recent development, rosenthal noted that these differences may offer clues about cardiovascular aging in humans. Heart disease tends to become more common in women after menopause, while its development in men generally follows a more gradual pattern. The distinct cellular changes observed in male and female mice could help researchers investigate the biological processes behind these differences.

However, the results describe differences in molecular activity, not demonstrated differences in heart function or disease risk. Further research will be needed to determine how these patterns influence cardiovascular health.

To explore whether their findings might also apply to people, the team compared the mouse results with previously published data from human hearts. Several molecular processes associated with aging, including pathways involved in responding to cellular stress, appeared in both species. This overlap suggests that at least some of the biological changes identified in mice may also be relevant to human heart aging.

"Our findings change the focus from aging across the entire heart to specific anatomical hotspots, helping us better understand how inflammation and fibrosis are connected and which regions of the heart are involved in the aging process," remarked study author Amalia Sintou, a postdoctoral associate at JAX.

Could These Discoveries Help Protect Aging Hearts?

Although the research does not yet identify a upcoming treatment, it offers scientists a more detailed understanding of where aging-related changes occur and which cells are involved. By revealing these cellular patterns, the findings could help guide future studies aimed at reducing cardiovascular decline, maintaining healthy heart function, and improving health later in life.

Rosenthal's team is now examining whether exercise, diet, and disease alter the interactions between immune cells and connective tissue cells. The researchers hope to distinguish the normal effects of aging from changes that may leave the heart increasingly vulnerable to cardiovascular problems.

The experimental design also helped the team isolate aging itself as a contributing factor. Because the mice lived under the same conditions and received the same diet, the researchers could investigate age-related changes without the additional variation introduced by different environments or eating habits.

"Valve replacement is common in older adults, and one of the big questions is how much of the underlying damage is driven by aging itself," noted study author Aleksandra Aljakna Khan, a postdoctoral associate at JAX. "Because all of the mice in our study lived in the same environment and ate the same diet, we were able to isolate the effects of aging and show that aging alone can initiate some of these changes in the valves and aorta.".

It has been revealed that together, the findings suggest that understanding heart aging requires looking beyond the muscle responsible for pumping blood. The valves, major blood vessels, and supporting cells may play a much larger role than previously recognized. Learning how these structures change and communicate over time could eventually help scientists identify ways to preserve cardiovascular health as people age.

Research Funding and Study Authors.

Sources indicate that the research received funding from the NIH Common Fund through The Jackson Laboratory Senescence Tissue Mapping Center (JAX-Sen TMC U54 AG079753). Additional support came from JAX's National Cancer Institute-designated Cancer Center (P30 CA034196).

Additional authors from The Jackson Laboratory included Yue Zhao, Antonios Somarakis, Harshpreet Chandok, Juliana Alcoforado Diniz, Ramalakshmi Ramasamy, Gretchen T. Clark, Brian S. White, Paul Robson, Ron Korstanje, and J. Matthew Mahoney. Leon Frommer and Sikander Hayat of RWTH Aachen University also contributed to the study.

Recent findings suggest that everyone at Car and Driver loves a road trip, and it’s clear that our editors play favorites when choosing a long-term car for said road trips. Often when traveling, an editor is rolling deep with family, friends, pets, and gear, so one of our more spacious vehicles usually ends up going along for the ride. With a few large cars at our disposal, the team has options, but after 20,000 miles, it’s clear that our long-term Hyundai Palisade Hybrid tends to be the first choice.

Since our last update around the 10,000-mile mark, the Palisade has seen shorter trips to Elk Rapids and Traverse City in Michigan, as well as to Cedar Point in Ohio, but it’s also made it as far as Colorado and West Virginia. Deputy video editor Carlos Lago loaded the Hyundai with his family, their dog, a travel crib, a dog bed, and luggage, and the Palisade Hybrid handled it all without glitch. In the logbook, Lago noted that the Palisade was “smooth, decently powerful, and adept at maintaining the higher freeway speeds up north, though the road and tire noise was louder than I’d like at those speeds.”.

See all results for newly introduced 2026 Hyundai Palisade Hybrid for sale near 41822.

Entry and exit haven’t proved as smooth as the Palisade’s ride, though. Lago—and other editors, including yours truly—bemoaned the hands-free door access, which will occasionally lock the doors instead of unlocking them. At that point, we just pull out the key fob, eliminating the point of that tech entirely.

The Palisade Hybrid’s largely white interior is another point of contention for staffers with kids, friends, and pets that ride in the back seat. Those of us with young children in car seats, particularly rear-facing ones, cringe at the footprints and mess we know is coming. Senior features editor Greg Fink hopped in at around 15,000 miles and wondered, “Is it just me, or is this interior looking a little worse for the wear?” With 20,000 miles still to go, we’re hoping that wear stays within reason.

Sources indicate that testing director Dave VanderWerp thought the Palisade Hybrid was a fantastic family SUV with a lot of features not available in other competitive SUVs, but he was still frustrated by parts of the road-trip experience. He found the cargo hold lacking capacity with the third row in use, though his teenagers did manage to occupy that row comfortably. Folding and unfolding the second row proved tricky for VanderWerp’s passengers. A recall on those seats may have added some difficulty there.

Technical editor Austin Irwin had high praise for the Palisade’s interior: “You can just about close your eyes and imagine you’re driving a Genesis.” That being said, he wasn’t blown away by the hybrid powertrain on the highway, where it was flipping between EV and internal-combustion propulsion too often.

Industry observers note that technical assistant Christi VanSyckle drove the Palisade Hybrid out to Colorado with her husband, daughter, and dogs in tow. “Even after a 15-hour driving day,” she wrote, “the comfort and ride were impressive the entire time.” However, her passengers also had issues stowing the second-row captain’s chairs, choosing instead to just squeeze past them to access the third row. VanSyckle called out the Palisade’s steering during her road trip, appreciating its heft when the going got mountainous.

See all results for latest 2026 Hyundai Palisade Hybrid for sale near 41822.

Since the last upgrade, the Palisade took one trip to the dealer for its routine 16,000-mile service, which included an oil and filter change, a tire rotation, and the usual inspections. The cabin filter also should have been replaced, per the vehicle’s maintenance schedule, but for some reason, the dealer decided not to change that out. As is, the total for that visit came out to $164.

While we can certainly find tidbits that annoy us (we’re very good at that), our long-term Hyundai Palisade Hybrid doesn’t seem like it will be dethroned as the regent of road trips anytime soon. With 20,000 miles left, perhaps we’ll even be able to figure out how the second-row seats work.

Going up north in Michigan often involves running the gamut of wild game crossing your path. With summer finally here, our trips up north have increased, as has our usage of the Hyundai Palisade Hybrid. Most of the fauna has been completely avoidable—with one exception.

Industry observers note that our 2026 Palisade Hybrid is equipped with factory built-in dash cams in the front and rear of the vehicle. They feature continuous-loop recording and parked motion/impact detection. The footage is stored to a MicroSD card. You can access the footage from the infotainment display and are able to look back at about two weeks' worth of clips (important to remember when you have this SUV in your possession).

Our most interesting recent clip came from managing testing editor David Beard, on his way up to Bear Lake, Michigan. A small bear crossed the Palisade Hybrid's path and didn't quite make it across before the right front corner of the SUV tagged it. Thanks to Beard's speedy reaction time, he slowed the SUV enough that it came away without any damage. As for the bear? At the time, we weren't quite sure. Would you check on a potentially very angry bear in the dead of night? A return trip the following day revealed that everyone appeared to make it out the unfortunate situation unscathed.

Beyond its ability to dodge live animals, the Palisade Hybrid has proven to be a great road-trip SUV. Many of our staffers cannot stop raving about the interior of this fresh Palisade. Vehicle testing director Dave VanderWerp stated it's "comfortable, quiet, and seriously upscale." Buyer's Guide director (and current Genesis owner) Rich Ceppos thinks that "this is a full-fledged luxury car now, good enough to wear a Genesis badge. The ride is creamy, the powertrain smooth and quiet, the interior plush, and infotainment straightforward. It's a properly coddling driving experience." Sarah Taylor, online production assistant, agreed that the interior is comfortable and luxurious and further pointed to the Palisade's smooth ride. She also noted: "Slim A-pillars are much appreciated: no huge blind spots." Buyer's Guide managing editor Drew Dorian, who hauled some friends down to Cedar Point in Ohio, praised the seats. He said, "The adjustable side bolsters are a nice touch, and I even found our long-termer's kinetic seat feature useful after four days of riding rollercoasters.".

However, there have been a couple small gripes along the way. VanderWerp thought that the Palisade Hybrid "feels substantially larger and less wieldy than the previous model behind the wheel." And despite all the features it has, the Hyundai is missing one key capability: You cannot lock/unlock the rear doors with a touch of the door handle. That's "something every parent of small children would use daily," he mentioned. As a mom of two handling no less than a purse, backpack, water bottle, and certainly a coffee mug at any given time, I fully agree.

It has been revealed that at around 8400 miles, it was time for the Palisade Hybrid to head to the dealer for routine service. This visit included an oil change, tire rotation, and multipoint inspection for a total of $146. In addition, there was an open recall that needed to be addressed. Recall 297 pertains to the third-row seatbelt and wiring harness. If the third-row seatbelt is promptly pulled and creates sudden tension, the internal wiring harness could break or become unseated. Luckily, we had not experienced this problem. The dealer inspected the belt buckle and then installed a wiring harness extension to relieve the tension, which was all covered under warranty. Speaking of recalls and seats, our Palisade also got an over-the-air-update fix for the unfortunate glitch with the power second- and third-row seats that initially had inadequate pinch detection and caused a brief stop-sale for the newly introduced Palisade.

With another 30,000 miles to go, there's no telling where the Palisade Hybrid will take us next. Wherever it goes, we hope the on-board cameras don't pick up any more encounters with bears—or other wildlife.

In a recent development, hybrids continue popping up in greater numbers across the three-row SUV segment, and one such flower has grown tall enough to catch our eye rather rapidly. After Hyundai introduced the redesigned Palisade for 2026, we snagged the upcoming hybrid variant for our annual 10Best competition, where it became an instant favorite. We decided to bring in the new award winner for an in-depth 40,000-mile evaluation.

We ended up with the top-trim Palisade Hybrid Calligraphy model, which starts at a modest $60,380, including the $2000 upcharge for all-wheel drive. Under the hood lies a turbocharged 2.5-liter inline-four and two electric motors nestled within the standard six-speed automatic transmission. Since the Calligraphy is the Palisade's poshest trim, its list of standard equipment is pretty long, including all manner of active safety equipment, rain-sensing wipers, nappa-leather seats with massage for the driver, a tow hitch, a digital rearview mirror, power-adjustable second-row seats, and a head-up display. The only added option on the car was a $245 set of carpeted floor mats, bringing our Palisade Hybrid's total to $60,625.

Our initial testing brought in some respectable numbers for this large hybrid, which produces 329 horsepower and 339 pound-feet of torque. The SUV hustled to 60 mph in 6.6 seconds. Top-gear passing from 50 to 70 mph took place in a tidy 4.4 seconds, and the Palisade sprinted through the quarter-mile in 15.0 seconds at 94 mph. It managed 0.84 g of lateral grip around the skidpad (more than most families will need) and required just 170 feet to stop from 70 mph.

Unfortunately, it didn't take long for our latest long-termer to hit a snag. Upon receiving our upcoming Palisade Hybrid, we began our normal long-term onboarding process, which consists of removing the wheels and measuring the thickness of the brake pads. When we went to remove the pads, we found a wheel stud that was already stripped and spinning in place. The Palisade was promptly whisked away to the dealer and then disappeared for two months. Upon its return, we learned the dealer had to drill out the wheel stud and replace the damaged wheel hub. Ouch.

In a recent development, from there, it took only two weeks before another problem popped up: The engine started overheating. As soon as the car reached higher speeds—especially on the highway—the dashboard would launch into a series of chimes and warnings alerting us that the engine temperature was nearing the danger zone. The Hyundai went back to the dealer, who informed us that the water-pump belt had shredded itself alive. A upcoming belt was installed, attachment points were tightened down, and we were assured it shouldn't happen again.

In a recent development, the dealer also took care of a few recalls and service bulletins that had cropped up. The service department replaced front-bumper wiring related to the active front air flaps and installed two software updates, one of which was required to prevent potential instrument-cluster failure. All repairs and recalls were done under warranty at no cost.

Industry observers note that since the Palisade Hybrid returned for a second time, we've had no further concerns. It went on a spring-break road trip to South Carolina and got back with no problems. We are hoping for more of the same as we rack up the miles on this well-dressed family hauler.

Vitamin B12 may hold the key to treating a rare genetic disorder

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A surprising discovery involving vitamin B12 could open new possibilities for understanding and potentially treating rare genetic disorders.
  • According to recent reports, the findings center on a cellular process called RNA splicing, which helps prepare the genetic instructions cells use to produce proteins.
  • Mutations in genes responsible for splicing can cause conditions such as Verheij syndrome.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A surprising discovery involving vitamin B12 could open new possibilities for understanding and potentially treating rare genetic disorders. Researchers found that the vitamin can correct developmental problems in tiny worms carrying a genetic mutation associated with Verheij syndrome, a rare human condition that causes developmental delays, impaired growth, and short stature.

According to recent reports, the findings center on a cellular process called RNA splicing, which helps prepare the genetic instructions cells use to produce proteins. During splicing, unnecessary portions of messenger RNA are removed, and the remaining sections are joined together in the correct order. When this process goes wrong, it can disrupt essential cellular functions and contribute to serious developmental disorders.

Mutations in genes responsible for splicing can cause conditions such as Verheij syndrome. To better understand the effects of these genetic changes, scientists investigated how a related mutation affects growth and metabolism in a laboratory model.

Vitamin B12 Reverses Developmental Defects in Worms.

Recent findings suggest that the discovery emerged from experiments involving C. elegans, a tiny roundworm commonly used in biological research. The researchers were initially searching for previously unknown genes that influence lifespan when they began examining a mutation in a gene involved in RNA splicing. The same gene is associated with Verheij syndrome in humans.

Sources indicate that worms carrying the mutation developed problems resembling key features of the human disorder. Their growth slowed considerably, and they remained smaller than normal.

Industry observers note that to investigate why this happened, the scientists conducted genetic screens and analyzed the worms' metabolism. They discovered that the mutation disrupted specific metabolic pathways that depend on vitamin B12 and are essential for healthy growth and normal cellular activity.

The researchers then tested whether providing additional vitamin B12 could counteract these changes. Remarkably, the treatment restored the affected metabolic processes to normal and corrected the developmental abnormalities associated with the mutation.

"We were surprised to find that a change in a fundamental process of RNA processing had such a targeted effect on vitamin B12-dependent metabolism," indicates Jonathan Kölschbach, first author of the study. "Even more exciting was that we were able to largely correct the consequences of this change in the worm model using vitamin B12.".

Could Vitamin B12 Help Treat a Rare Genetic Disorder?

To explore whether their findings might also apply to people, the researchers examined publicly available datasets from human cells. They also worked with Hormos Dafsari, a neuropediatrician at the University Hospital Cologne, to collect blood samples from patients diagnosed with Verheij syndrome.

These investigations uncovered evidence of similar metabolic changes in humans, suggesting that the vitamin B12-related pathways affected in the worms may also play a role in the human disorder.

It has been revealed that although the results are promising, researchers have not yet established whether vitamin B12 supplementation can improve symptoms in people with Verheij syndrome. Additional studies will be necessary to determine whether the benefits observed in worms can be translated into a treatment for patients.

According to recent reports, the discovery also raises a broader possibility. Metabolic disruptions may contribute more substantially to diseases caused by faulty RNA splicing than scientists previously recognized. Understanding these connections could help researchers identify new therapeutic strategies, potentially extending beyond Verheij syndrome to other rare genetic conditions.

Industry observers note that "Our study is a good example of how basic research on model organisms can provide new insights into human diseases," notes Adam Antebi, Director at the Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing and lead author of the study. "A fundamental biological question can thus give rise to a new approach that could also become medically relevant in the long term.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Nova was unveiled at RE+ in Las Vegas this week, and it’s already in production at Megafactory 1, the battery-repurposing plant that Moment Energy opened in the Vancouver area in June.
  • According to recent reports, each Nova unit delivers 500 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of energy and 200 kilowatts (kW) of power.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A retired EV battery can still have years of use left in it when it’s taken off the road. Moment Energy’s upcoming Nova battery storage system puts those packs to work on commercial sites. And when a pack wears out, it can be swapped without pulling out the whole system.

Nova was unveiled at RE+ in Las Vegas this week, and it’s already in production at Megafactory 1, the battery-repurposing plant that Moment Energy opened in the Vancouver area in June.

According to recent reports, each Nova unit delivers 500 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of energy and 200 kilowatts (kW) of power. It has a 2.94 m by 1.80 m (9.7 x 5.9 ft) footprint, and units can be linked together for projects in the tens of megawatt-hours. A site could charge the batteries when electricity is cheaper or when its solar panels are producing more than it needs, then draw on that power when demand spikes or the grid goes down.

Nova can use packs from different EV models, even when those packs have aged at different rates. Moment’s battery management software tracks how each pack is doing. As packs wear out, the company can replace them while leaving the enclosure and concrete pad in place. Moment notes its pack replacement service could keep a system in service for more than 20 years.

“We see a future where reengineered EV batteries become essential infrastructure for powering businesses and onshoring manufacturing and supply chains. Nova brings that vision to life, combining safety, engineering, and North American manufacturing to deploy the safest and highest-performance batteries ever made: EV batteries to supercharge our aging grid,” noted Edward Chiang, co-founder and CEO of Moment Energy.

It has been revealed that moment Energy claims Nova is the first storage system built from retired EV batteries to earn both UL 1973 certification for the batteries and UL 9540 certification for the complete system. It was also tested under UL 9540A, which looks at how a battery fire can spread. The factory itself is certified under UL 1974, which covers how used batteries are assessed and graded for reuse.

In a recent development, that matters for businesses with limited space. Nova is designed to sit outdoors alongside the buildings it serves. It uses liquid cooling, detects smoke, heat, and flammable gases, and is rated to operate from −13F to 122F (−25C to 50C).

Moment Energy also says an independent review found that Nova meets US federal sourcing restrictions tied to the clean electricity investment tax credit. Those rules are one part of determining whether a project qualifies for the credit.

Orders are open, and Moment Energy expects the first units to ship in Q1 2027 for deployments across North America.

Kimi Antonelli took pole for the Las Vegas Grand Prix by being the last of the contenders to start their final flying lap in Q3. With a five-place grid drop, the new F1 champion will start Saturday night’s Grand Prix from sixth.

Max Verstappen, who held provisional pole until the final flurry of attempts, will inherit the P1 starting spot, and George Russell will start second after qualifying third.

Russell, by far the fastest in Friday’s practice, asked the Mercedes pit wall if he could have a tow, knowing Mercedes was the clear frontrunner and his champion teammate was destined to start further back in the field.

Mercedes didn’t oblige, and both drivers entered the waiting game with the rest of the contenders, as no one wanted to be the first driver out for the final lap, punching through the frigid cold air of the Las Vegas desert alone.

Sources indicate that ultimately, Verstappen went first and did not improve on his first Q3 time, which was still good enough for an elevated front-row starting spot. Antonelli crossed the line to start his lap with a second remaining.

It has been revealed that lando Norris will start third after qualifying fourth ahead of Isack Hadjar and Arvid Lindblad. Oscar Piastri found himself in a familiar starting position of seventh but faces a 10-place grid penalty.

With rain on Thursday and a dry forecast for every session of consequence during the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend, most contenders first saw what their new 2027 cars had during FP3 on Friday, ahead of qualifying.

Neither Ferrari made it to Q3, settling for 11th and 12th as neither Lewis Hamilton nor Charles Leclerc put themselves in position to give the other a tow.

Nico Hulkenberg, Carlos Sainz, Gabriel Bortoleto, and Alex Albon were knocked out in Q2.

According to recent reports, haas reserve driver Rafael Camara nearly made it to Q2 in his second F1 qualifying attempt but was knocked out at the last minute by the Audis. He joined Sergio Perez, Fernando Alonso, Lance Stroll, Valtteri Bottas, and Ollie Bearman.

According to recent reports, I have to admit that when I first saw the Fangchengbao Tai 9 stow its steering wheel away on social media, I assumed that it was AI. It wasn't. This BYD brand's fresh SUV can indeed retract its steering wheel right into the dashboard. However, it’s not quite used for the reason you’d think.

Sources indicate that the Tai 9 is a six-seat, plug-in hybrid SUV about the same size as the Cadillac Escalade IQ, and it sits at the top of the Fangchengbao range. BYD’s Chinese-market brand and naming structure can be confusing, but in essence, Fangchengbao is one of BYD's premium brands.

Sources indicate that power comes from two electric motors that produce 536 horsepower at peak, while a 1.5-liter turbocharged engine is responsible for any combustion-powered driving. The Tai 9 has a 66.5 kWh battery that is capable of BYD’s flash charging technology. The brand claims it can sprint from 10% to 97% in nine minutes.

Sources indicate that those are all very compelling specs, but the most interesting part of the Tai 9 is the top-of-the-line Foldable Smart Cabin trim. Since the Tai 9 uses a steer-by-wire system, the steering wheel can fold up and stow itself in the dashboard. BYD says that takes about 10 seconds.

Sources indicate that however, this isn’t for any sort of autonomous driving. China’s autonomous driving rules are strict, and no automaker in the country has approval for commercially sold eyes-off, hands-off driver assist features. Instead, the folding steering wheel is primarily for comfort and space, specifically when the car is stationary. Photos of the feature in action show that stowing away the steering wheel makes extra room for a little table setup.

According to recent reports, this isn’t entirely unprecedented. The new trend in China is for large SUVs to be third spaces where buyers can comfortably hang out, even when they aren't driving. The Tai 9’s Nappa leather, comfy seats, and second-row folding screen are meant to make it a calming, relaxing space to spend time. It's similar in concept to what we’ve seen on the Zeekr Mix and SkyNomad N90 Studio.

Still, despite the Tai 9’s folding steering wheel not being for self-driving, I wouldn’t be surprised if it does show up in cars for that reason someday, as manufacturers strive to make cars that can truly drive themselves.

A car with no steering wheel at all might feel risky and uncomfortable to some car buyers, especially if it's like Tesla’s Cybercab, which can’t be driven manually at all above low speeds. Yet, if there were a backup to take control, I could see that putting some minds at ease.

The Fangchengbao Tai 9 is on sale in China for about $42,000. The top-of-the-line model with the foldable steering wheel is about $49,500.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Upgrade 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

It has been revealed that patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller patch. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

In a recent development, the patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

In a recent development, the end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Sources indicate that interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

The other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

In a recent development, and, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Sources indicate that finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD is preparing to launch a fresh flagship MPV soon after previewing the large people mover for the first time.

We knew it was coming soon after images of the camouflaged multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) began flooding the internet last month.

Zhang Zhuo, general manager of BYD’s Ocean sales division, confirmed the newly introduced flagship MPV is coming soon.

“A new creation for the times, born for the family,” Zhuo said after posting a preview of it for the first time on his Weibo account on Friday.

In a recent development, the fresh flagship Ocean MPV is “coming soon,” according to Zhuo, but he didn’t reveal a specific debut date. He previously mentioned the firm expects to launch its first MPV under the Ocean lineup by the end of 2026, so local reports suggest it will make an official debut next week at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto show, which kicks off on November 27.

Although it’s blurred, the preview highlights a similar shape and size to the recent spy images, with a roof-mounted LiDAR and traditional pull-style door handles.

It doesn’t appear to look much like the futuristic Ocean-V concept BYD unveiled at the 2026 Beijing Auto Show earlier this year, a preview of its first MPV under the Ocean series.

The concept featured a sliding center display screen and two different modes: Camping and Movie. In camping mode, the seats either fold flat to create a bed or swivel to face each other.

In Movie mode, the vehicle transforms into a private mobile theater with a large display screen that flips out of the dashboard.

While it may not have some of the more extravagant elements from the concept, the Ocean MPV is expected to be “flagship-worthy,” if you will, with BYD’s latest tech and other premium features like zero-gravity seats and plenty of digital screens.

The Ocean-V’s innovations “will gradually make their way into mass-production vehicles,” BYD mentioned earlier this year.

BYD has yet to announce any details, but the flagship Ocean MPV is expected to be about the size of the Xia, a large plug-in hybrid minivan sold under its Dynasty lineup.

The BYD Xia measures 5,145 mm long, 1,970 mm wide, and 1,805 mm tall, with a 3,045 mm wheelbase.

Like the Xia, the Ocean MPV is expected to use BYD’s latest-generation DM-i plug-in hybrid system with a 1.5L engine and a 200 kW electric motor.

In a recent development, the Xia starts at 249,800 yuan ($37,500) in China. It’s available with two BYD Blade LFP battery packs: 20.4 kWh and 36.6 kWh, providing pure electric CLTC ranges of 100 km (62 miles) and 218 km (135 miles). On a full tank of gas and full charge, the plug-in people mover offers a combined CLTC range of 1,163 km (722 miles).

Sources indicate that BYD also sells the flagship Denza D9 MPV under its luxury sub-brand. With the Denza D9 starting above 300,000 yuan and the Xia at around 250,000 yuan, the Ocean MPV is expected to fill the gap.

Zhuo noted to stay tuned for more coming soon, so check back for updates.

#86960. Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (960 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, as quantum computers grow more powerful, researchers face a troubling question: How can they know whether the results are correct when conventional computers can no longer verify them?
  • The technique uses experimental measurements to reconstruct how a quantum system behaves, then calculates how uncertainties in that reconstruction affect the results.
  • Quantum systems are expected to become capable of solving increasingly complex problems that traditional computers struggle with or cannot handle at all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, as quantum computers grow more powerful, researchers face a troubling question: How can they know whether the results are correct when conventional computers can no longer verify them? Scientists have now developed a promising fresh method that could help overcome this challenge by measuring the accuracy of quantum simulations and identifying how much uncertainty their predictions contain.

The technique uses experimental measurements to reconstruct how a quantum system behaves, then calculates how uncertainties in that reconstruction affect the results. Researchers successfully demonstrated the approach using a quantum simulator with up to 51 qubits in Innsbruck, Austria.

Quantum systems are expected to become capable of solving increasingly complex problems that traditional computers struggle with or cannot handle at all. However, this progress creates a verification problem. When a simulation is small enough, scientists can compare its results with calculations performed on a conventional computer. As quantum systems grow beyond those limits, that direct comparison becomes impractical, making alternative ways to assess their reliability essential.

A Fresh Way to Measure Quantum Computing Accuracy.

Sources indicate that the breakthrough comes from an international research team led by Tristan Kraft at the Technical University of Munich and Peter Zoller at the University of Innsbruck and the Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information of the Austrian Academy of Sciences, working alongside Barbara Kraus of the Technical University of Munich. The researchers developed a method for experimentally determining how a quantum simulator operates and translating uncertainties in its behavior into measurable limits on the accuracy of its results.

Industry observers note that quantum simulators are specialized physical systems designed to reproduce the behavior of other quantum systems. They are especially useful for investigating situations involving large numbers of interacting particles, where the calculations required can rapidly overwhelm even powerful conventional computers.

But quantum experiments are never entirely free from errors. "But no real experiment is perfect," claims Tristan Kraft. "Interactions may turn out differently than expected, the system is influenced by its environment, and measurements are also subject to uncertainties.".

Rather than assuming a quantum simulator behaves exactly as intended, the new approach examines experimental data to determine what is actually happening inside the system. This allows researchers to identify key interactions and account for disturbances such as fluctuations and noise.

"From this data, we determine the relevant interactions as well as key influences from fluctuations and noise. We then calculate how the uncertainties in this model affect the simulation results," explains Tristan Kraft. "The quantum simulator thus provides not just a single value, but a result with error margins that quantify its accuracy.".

Successfully Tested on a 51 Qubit Quantum Simulator.

Sources indicate that to evaluate the method, the researchers began with a relatively small quantum system containing ten trapped ions. Because conventional computers can still calculate the behavior of a system of this size, the team could test its reconstructed models and calculated error limits against independent measurements.

After this initial validation, the researchers expanded their experiments to a chain of 51 trapped ions. The larger demonstration, carried out by a team led by Manoj Joshi and Christian Roos using an ion trap quantum simulator, highlighted that the technique could also work with substantially more complex quantum systems.

This represents an important step toward establishing how trustworthy quantum simulation results are, particularly as quantum devices advance into territory where direct verification with traditional computing methods becomes increasingly difficult.

Extending the Breakthrough to More Complex Quantum Systems.

It has been revealed that the next challenge is to bring the technique to two-dimensional quantum simulators. These systems can model more complicated interactions among particles, making them valuable for exploring quantum physics. At the same time, their growing complexity makes their results particularly difficult to confirm using conventional calculations.

"This is particularly key because classical calculations for such systems become significantly more difficult as the number of particles increases," explains quantum computing pioneer Peter Zoller. "This also makes independent verification of the results increasingly complex, making the question of experimentally determined error limits all the more important.".

The researchers are now adapting their method for the newest generation of two-dimensional quantum simulators, which offer improved precision and can investigate systems containing larger numbers of particles.

Industry observers note that looking further ahead, the approach could help scientists establish a more meaningful way to measure quantum advantage, the ability of quantum systems to outperform conventional computers. Instead of comparing machines based only on their processing speed or the size of the problems they can handle, researchers could also examine how accurately each system produces its answers.

"After all, when a classical computer and a quantum simulator tackle the same problem, it's not just a matter of which one delivers a result faster. What's also crucial is which one can solve the problem with a smaller, verifiable margin of error," says Peter Zoller.

This shift could change how progress in quantum computing is evaluated. Future breakthroughs may be judged not simply by how many particles a simulator can model or how quickly it performs calculations, but by its ability to solve increasingly difficult problems with demonstrably reliable results.

Sources indicate that the findings were published in Physical Review X. The research received support from the Austrian Science Fund (FWF), the German Ministry of Research, Technology and Space, the European Union, BMW, and other funding organizations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Max Verstappen and George Russell start side by side on the front row for the Las Vegas Grand Prix Saturday evening, thanks to a five-place grid penalty for pole-sitter and world champion Kimi Antonelli.

With this front row, there is no love lost over their careers and, more specifically, this weekend, as Russell enters the race upset, with a first step in following the clash between the two and FP3, in which Russell rebounded to top the time charts with a time of 1:34.805.

In a recent development, in FP3, Verstappen passed Russell and, in the next corner, braked hard, forcing the Mercedes driver to run off the racing line and towards the barrier in an evasive maneuver. Following the brake, the two banged wheels in a session without consequence. After the light collision, Verstappen flipped off Russell on the next straight. The drivers were called in front of the stewards, and Verstappen was given a warning after being found to have made an “unpredictable change of direction under braking.”.

It has been revealed that this was the third time during FP3 that Verstappen pulled such a move, as he was already under investigation for doing the same to the Alpine of Franco Colapinto and the McLaren of Lando Norris. Russell’s woes with Verstappen’s move this week is that he finds that the four-time champion has a pattern of behavior that screws over those he’s competing against. In this case overtaking at the start of a practice lap.

With FP3 being the only dry practice sessions of the weekend, emotions were elevated as drivers were pressed to figure out how the new car works on the coldest street circuit of the year.

Recent findings suggest that “There’s nothing in the rules that claims you cannot overtake someone who is starting a lap but you’re screwing this person over,” Russell stated post race to sky sports Italia. “He does this week in and week out with many drivers and everyone accepts it.

“I’m not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they’re bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody’s got to stand up to this guy.”.

When the comments were shared with Verstappen, he brushed them off, saying he wasn’t going to waste his time on the comments before adding that in racing there are no gentleman’s agreements.

“I've never heard of a gentleman’s agreement in my life, Verstappen said.

Mercedes Team Principal Toto Wolff told Sky Sports that, with his driver and his Red Bull advisory on the front row, we should expect cinema if they go for the same line into the opening corner of the Grand Prix tonight.

“If they try to go through the first corners together, we shall be watching,” Wolff said.

This is the first time this year that the two start next to each other on the front row and the ninth across their careers.

Tesla officially introduced in Argentina on Friday with President Javier Milei on stage in Buenos Aires, and Elon Musk joined by video from his plane to welcome the brand’s newest market. It didn’t go well.

Musk got through one line about Tesla before stalling out: “Sorry, I don’t really know what I want to say.” The call ended about two minutes in, without any real pitch for the Model 3 or Model Y that Tesla had just put on sale.

It has been revealed that the launch took place at Arenas Studio in Buenos Aires’ La Boca neighborhood. Milei spoke for less than eight minutes, then the host asked the room to welcome “our next guest,” and Musk popped up on the giant screen from what looked like an airplane cabin. Milei burst out laughing and bounced on his feet.

Industry observers note that musk started fine: “Hello, Argentina. Well, here we are. It’s a joy to share Tesla with all of you and to establish ourselves there.”.

JAJAJAJ QUE ES ESTO, Milei lo llamó de sorpresa a Elon Musk para que diga algo sobre el local de Tesla inaugurado y es lo mas INCÓMODO que vas a ver en tu vida, se quería ir a la mierda y COLGÓ, durísimo, ni Elon Musk lo soporta al gordo pelotudo pic.twitter.com/CrJkv4iu1x.

Sources indicate that then he started glancing off to each side. “Actually, I don’t really know what to say, other than thank you for this welcome to Tesla in Argentina,” he mentioned. He briefly mentioned a charging network with state-owned oil manufacturer YPF, thanked the audience again, and then: “Sorry, I don’t really know what I want to say.”.

And that was it. The feed cut before he even said goodbye.

Milei tried to save it. Back on stage, he told the crowd that “those who do a lot, talk little,” and called Musk “the Leonardo da Vinci of the 21st century.”.

The clip is now spreading fast in Argentina, with one post of the video racking up over 1.1 million views overnight.

Tesla opened online orders on Friday for five versions of the Model 3 and Model Y, all imported from Gigafactory Shanghai. Here are the list prices, VAT included:.

It has been revealed that tesla adds about $600 in reservation, destination, and documentation fees on top of that, and first deliveries aren’t expected until March or April 2027. There are no dealers. Sales happen online, with showroom space at the Unicenter and Alcorta Shopping malls in Buenos Aires.

It has been revealed that argentina is Tesla’s fourth direct-sales market in South America after Chile, Colombia, and Uruguay, which launched in July. Tesla is late to the party, though. BYD already leads Argentina’s EV market after Milei’s government cut import taxes on electric vehicles.

That was awkward. Like, really awkward.

What I really found awkward was hearing Musk stating "I'm not MAGA, I'm not sure what MAGA means" in his interview with CNBC.

Especially surprising after he declared, "I’m not just MAGA; I’m 'Dark MAGA,'" after spending half a billion dollars to support MAGA candidates, and after promoting the MAGA political agenda (which he has, in part, personally implemented through the DOGE).

At this point, I expect him to reappear in the guise of a Democrat and write a big, fat, one-billion-dollar check to a Democratic super PAC for the 2028 election cycle.

I am sure Musk has a lot on his mind right now, but selling Tesla vehicles clearly isn’t one of them, because he couldn’t come up with anything to say about it.

Launching a newly introduced market has one job: get people excited to buy the cars. Musk had a sitting president cheering for him on stage, a room full of fans, and every camera in Buenos Aires pointed at him. He couldn’t come up with a single reason to buy a Model Y.

This isn’t stage fright. Musk has been telling investors for two years that Tesla’s future is robotaxis and Optimus robots, not selling cars. Meanwhile, Tesla’s deliveries fell 8.6% to 1.636 million in 2025, its second annual decline in a row. The guy who is behind the brand doesn’t care about selling these cars anymore, and this clip shows it better than anything I’ve seen.

This Plug-In Hybrid SUV Towed A Boeing 747 On Only 2 Wheels. Yes, Really.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, BYD is one of the many Chinese car companies trying to rack up orders, and its Denza brand has now recreated a famous Volkswagen commercial from two decades ago that involved a diesel-powered SUV and a jumbo jet.
  • According to recent reports, I vividly remember when I saw the original clip 20 years ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chinese automakers are trying to capture as much of the European car market as possible, and they’re resorting to clever marketing tricks that legacy automakers have used in the past to attract buyers.

In a recent development, BYD is one of the many Chinese car companies trying to rack up orders, and its Denza brand has now recreated a famous Volkswagen commercial from two decades ago that involved a diesel-powered SUV and a jumbo jet. Only this time, Denza has an ace up its sleeve, and it’s quite impressive.

According to recent reports, I vividly remember when I saw the original clip 20 years ago. A blue Volkswagen Touareg V10 diesel towed a 171-ton jet aircraft down the same Dunsfold runway in the United Kingdom where the old "Top Gear" episodes used to be filmed.

It has been revealed that now, the Denza B5 (or Bao 5 in some markets) plug-in hybrid SUV is back at the same place to do the same stunt, but adapted for a 2026 where everything seemingly needs to be bigger, more over the top, and more in-your-face. (I blame TikTok.).

Industry observers note that so, we have a Chinese PHEV that uses two electric motors and a 1.5-liter gas engine. It’s all-wheel-drive, its 31.8-kilowatt-hour battery can deliver up to 56 miles of all-electric range on a full battery, and it has two mechanical locking differentials. This last part is crucial. The battery can be fast-charged at up to 100 kW, and the total system output is a healthy 536 horsepower, with most of that oomph being provided by the two e-motors.

We also have a 207-ton jumbo jet that got a quick repositioning for no other purpose than pure entertainment.

Here comes the interesting bit: While Volkswagen’s original stunt kept all four of the Touareg’s wheels in place—you know, how a car usually works—BYD decided to put its PHEV SUV to the test by gradually removing some wheels.

Sources indicate that the first run was done with all four wheels in place, followed by a three-wheeled run with 2.2 tons of ballast. For the final act, both right wheels were removed, and the ballast reached 5 tonnes. During the three runs, the Denza B5 towed the Boeing 747-400 over one mile, and best of all, it used exclusively electric power.

It has been revealed that the point of it all? Promote the newly introduced SUV to the UK market, where the Land Rover Defender is among its biggest rivals. Unlike the Defender, however, which is now based on a unibody design and is primarily combustion-powered, the Denza B5 sits on a bespoke ladder-frame chassis and more substantially electrified. It has a gas engine that acts mainly as a generator for the high-voltage battery. The battery cells are directly integrated between the chassis rails.

According to recent reports, if you're thinking about trying this stunt at home, just know the vehicle needed a few modifications to pull it off. BYD added a custom towing attachment, removed some seats to make room for the ballast, and added stabilizers to make up for the missing wheels.

#86955. Electric cars are finally mainstream in GTA 6, and Vice City is full of them

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1341 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Electric cars are finally mainstream in GTA 6, and Vice City is full of them

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1341 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that electric vehicles have finally gone mainstream in Grand Theft Auto.
  • It’s a substantial change for a series that spent over a decade treating EVs as a Tesla joke.
  • According to recent reports, I’ve been playing GTA 6 since it debuted on Thursday, partly for fun and partly because I wanted to see how Rockstar would handle EVs this time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that electric vehicles have finally gone mainstream in Grand Theft Auto. In GTA 6, EVs are just part of everyday traffic in Vice City, from Tesla and Porsche lookalikes to a parody of Electrify America’s charging network.

It’s a substantial change for a series that spent over a decade treating EVs as a Tesla joke. After a few days of playing, I’d say Rockstar nailed the vibe.

According to recent reports, I’ve been playing GTA 6 since it debuted on Thursday, partly for fun and partly because I wanted to see how Rockstar would handle EVs this time. The answer: a lot better than I expected.

Recent findings suggest that the game starts you in the Keys, Rockstar’s take on the Florida Keys, and it’s a rougher part of Leonida. Lots of older cars and beaters, and you won’t see many EVs.

That changes as you head north to Vice City, the game’s version of Miami. The closer you get, the more electric cars show up in traffic, and the more charging stations you pass. By the time you’re in the city, EVs are just normal cars.

That’s pretty much how EV adoption looks in the real world, concentrated in big, wealthier metro areas while rural areas lag behind.

Here’s what I’ve run into so far:.

That last one got me. Gas cars blocking chargers has been a complaint for as long as public charging has existed, and we’ve covered EV owners blocking a gas station in protest over ICEing. Rockstar recreating it tells me someone at the studio has actually tried to charge an EV in public. Probably even in Florida, which they tried to recreate here.

GTA 6 is the first mainline GTA where energy matters. Gas cars burn fuel and need a pump, and EVs have a battery level and need a plug.

Rockstar could have used that to make EVs a pain. It didn’t. In my testing, the EVs have about the same range as the gas cars, charge just as fast as a fill-up, and cost the same or less to top up.

Recent findings suggest that kotaku’s range test backs that up. On the same highway loop, a Tesla Model 3 lookalike lasted 20 minutes and 23 seconds on a charge, longer than the Banshee sports car at 18 minutes and 31 seconds, and not far off an old pickup at 29 minutes and 8 seconds. Crossing the whole map by highway takes under 15 minutes, according to Kotaku.

Industry observers note that and finding a charger isn’t a problem. Wccftech counted 120 EV chargers marked on the map, against just 57 gas stations.

Rockstar’s EV history starts with Coil, the series’ Tesla stand-in, named after the Tesla coil. GTA V, released in 2013, gave us the Coil Voltic, a copy of the original Lotus-based Tesla Roadster, alongside oddballs like the Cheval Surge and the Fisker Karma-inspired Khamelion.

In a recent development, the Voltic was quick off the line and slow everywhere else. It had the lowest top speed of any supercar in the game, which fan lore pins on its battery overheating at speed. That’s pretty much how a lot of people thought about EVs in 2013.

GTA Online added more electric cars starting in late 2017: the Rimac-inspired Coil Cyclone, then the Model S-based Coil Raiden and the Taycan-inspired Pfister Neon around the Doomsday Heist update. That same update introduced Avon Hertz, a tech billionaire whose AI tries to end the world. Rockstar never said who he was based on. Players didn’t need the help.

But those were rare, expensive toys. Nothing in GTA V needed fuel, so an EV was just a gas car without the engine noise, and you mostly saw them in the garages of players who bought them.

Electrify America noticed its in-game twin fast. The Volkswagen-owned network put out a statement on Friday saying it “will stick to charging vehicles in the real world” and adding, “We wish ReVolt America well.”.

In a recent development, it’s a good-natured response, and probably the best free marketing the network has had in years. EA has spent most of the last decade fighting a reputation for broken chargers, even though reliability across US fast-charging networks has improved this year. Every ReVolt station I’ve used in the game worked. Not a perfect parody, then.

It has been revealed that GTA has always been a parody of American life. With EVs, it’s now slightly ahead of it.

Florida is one of the strongest EV markets in the country, with a 9.4% share of upcoming passenger vehicle sales in Q2 2026 versus 7.4% nationally, according to the Southern Alliance for Clean Energy. Electrify America alone runs more than 350 chargers at over 60 Florida stations, including its biggest station yet near Orlando’s theme parks.

It has been revealed that but real Florida still has roughly three gas stations for every public charging location, based on the Alliance for Automotive Innovation’s count of 3,267 charging locations and xMap’s count of more than 10,500 gas stations. Leonida flips that ratio.

There’s one piece Rockstar hasn’t nailed, at least not yet. You can’t install a charger at your place, but early in the story you’re renting. I’m not far enough in to own a property, so I don’t know whether that changes later.

It matters, because home charging is the biggest real-world advantage of an EV. Most owners leave every morning with a full battery and rarely use public chargers. If owned properties in GTA 6 come with a plug, EVs become the more convenient choice in the game, just like they are in real life for anyone with a driveway.

Recent findings suggest that I also haven’t hit a mission built around EVs yet. If I find one, I’ll revision this post.

GTA works as a mirror. In 2013, the EV was a punchline: a Tesla parody that overheated if you drove it too fast. In 2026, it’s just another car in Vice City traffic, and the joke is on the guy in the pickup parked in the charging stall.

That’s a good sign of where EVs actually are. Satire goes after what’s common, and Rockstar decided EVs are common enough to be part of everyday Leonida, more so in the city than in the Keys, just like real life. And that message is reaching a huge audience. Take-Two indicates GTA 6 did $3.79 billion in first-day sales. Tens of millions of people are now driving EVs that charge as fast and as cheaply as gas cars, with no range anxiety. No automaker ad campaign gets close to that.

Recent findings suggest that so EVs aren’t a statement in GTA anymore. They’re normal, which is exactly the point the industry has been trying to make for years.

The real Florida just needs to catch up.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that after the Clean Up After Donnie GTA 6 mission, Donnie becomes a fence you can sell narcotics, marked notes, and jewelry to, all you have to do is drop them in the deposit box at his trailer in Key Lento. But with Brian also a fence, you may be wondering whether it's more beneficial to sell your goods to Donnie or Brian. While one may offer more lucrative rewards, all that glitters isn't necessarily gold in GTA 6.

If you hover your cursor over a fencing location icon on the GTA 6 map, you can see the rate each respective fence is offering for narcotics, marked bills, and jewelry. In GTA 6 Chapter 1, Donnie (Donnie's Trailer) pays low for narcotics, and very low for jewelry and marked bills.

Brian (Brian's Lockup), on the other hand, pays very low for all three types of illicit products. As such, Donnie pays more than Brian for narcotics. For example, if you collect all the cocaine drops Cal tells you about after the Clean Up After Donnie mission and fence them, Donnie offers you $3,400, while Brian offers just $2,720. Do note that the time it takes for these payments to reach your mailbox can be impacted by any available missions.

Recent findings suggest that while Donnie pays more, Cal suggests you sell the cocaine drops you collect to Brian, by depositing them at Brian's Lockup in Key Lento. He doesn't say why, but he seems to know something you don't. You should listen to Cal and sell your goods to Brian as the events of a later mission, called Swamped, might impact any payments Donnie owes you in GTA 6 (be aware of major spoilers by following that link).

Note that if you sell to Brian and he seems to be taking his time to pay you, there may be an available Brian mission you must complete before your payment is sent to the mailbox at Jason's House.

#86953. Latest wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1040 w)

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Latest wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1040 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A fresh wearable patch could offer a surprisingly simple way to improve one of the most crucial stages of sleep, without relying on medication or surgery.
  • Known as NEUSLeeP, the soft patch attaches to the skin and combines ultrasound stimulation with electrodes that monitor brain activity in real time.
  • It has been revealed that REM sleep, short for rapid eye movement sleep, is the stage when most vivid dreaming occurs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A fresh wearable patch could offer a surprisingly simple way to improve one of the most crucial stages of sleep, without relying on medication or surgery. Developed by researchers led by the University of Texas at Austin, the device uses gentle ultrasound waves to stimulate regions deep inside the brain, helping people enter REM sleep sooner and spend more time in this restorative stage.

Known as NEUSLeeP, the soft patch attaches to the skin and combines ultrasound stimulation with electrodes that monitor brain activity in real time. This allows researchers to influence brain regions involved in sleep while simultaneously tracking how the brain responds.

It has been revealed that REM sleep, short for rapid eye movement sleep, is the stage when most vivid dreaming occurs. It also plays an key role in processing emotions, consolidating memories, and adapting to stress. Disturbances in this stage of sleep have been associated with several mental health conditions, making it an important target for fresh treatments.

"This is the first time we've been able to noninvasively target deep brain regions involved in REM sleep, while simultaneously monitoring brain activity," said Kai Wing "Kevin" Tang, a recent UT biomedical engineering Ph.D. graduate who led the research effort.

"Our skin-attached NEUSLeeP patch opens up new possibilities for understanding sleep and treating sleep disorders in home settings," added Huiliang "Evan" Wang, assistant professor in the Cockrell School of Engineering's Department of Biomedical Engineering. Wang supervised Tang's research and served as the principal investigator (PI) overseeing the project.

Sleep Patch Helps People Reach REM Sleep 43 Minutes Faster.

The early results suggest that the technology can make a measurable difference in how people experience REM sleep.

In a study involving 28 participants, published in Nature Communications, people using the patch entered REM sleep an average of 43 minutes sooner and spent approximately 16 additional minutes in that stage.

These improvements were observed in both healthy sleepers and participants experiencing certain sleep difficulties. The volunteers also reported that the patch was comfortable to wear, with minimal adverse effects.

Industry observers note that unlike medications that affect the body more broadly, NEUSLeeP is designed to deliver stimulation to specific brain regions involved in sleep regulation. It uses ultrasound, a form of sound energy with frequencies beyond human hearing, to reach areas beneath the surface of the brain without requiring an invasive procedure.

The findings are encouraging, although the relatively small study means that larger trials will be needed to determine how consistently the technology works and whether its benefits persist over time.

Potential Benefits for Stress and Emotional Health.

The researchers also found evidence that the patch's effects may extend beyond increasing REM sleep.

Among healthy participants, ultrasound stimulation improved heart rate variability, a measure of the natural differences in time between consecutive heartbeats. This measurement provides insight into how the body's nervous system responds to stress and adjusts to changing conditions.

It has been revealed that brain imaging revealed changes in neural circuits involved in emotional processing. Together, these findings suggest that improving REM sleep through targeted stimulation could potentially support emotional regulation and the ability to cope with stress.

"REM sleep is not just about dreaming -- it's about emotional reset and stress adaptation," explained Gregory Fonzo, assistant professor in the Dell Medical School's Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences and one of the project's co-PIs. "By enhancing REM, we may help people better cope with stress and improve their overall well-being.".

These possibilities are especially interesting because REM sleep disturbances have been linked to depression, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

It has been revealed that current approaches to sleep problems often involve medication or behavioral therapy. Although these treatments can be effective, medications may produce unwanted side effects, and existing approaches do not always directly address the biological processes responsible for disrupted REM sleep.

Industry observers note that A device capable of influencing those processes without drugs or surgery could therefore offer an additional treatment option. However, the researchers have not yet established whether NEUSLeeP can improve symptoms of mental health disorders.

A New Direction for Treating Insomnia and PTSD.

Building on the initial findings, the research team plans to conduct larger clinical trials to confirm the patch's effects and investigate its potential use in people with PTSD, depression, and chronic insomnia.

Beyond treating sleep disorders, the technology could eventually support sleep monitoring at home and provide scientists with a fresh way to study how deep brain regions influence sleep. Researchers also envision personalized therapies that could be adjusted to individual sleep patterns and needs.

It has been revealed that "Our vision is a future where patients with mental health disorders can optimize their sleep with a noninvasive and safe treatment," stated Vincent Mysliwiec, M.D., a professor at UT Health San Antonio, a leading expert in sleep disorders, and another co-PI on the project. "This technology could help millions of people get the restorative sleep they need.".

Recent findings suggest that the team is already taking steps toward making NEUSLeeP available beyond the research setting. Working with the university's commercialization unit, Discovery to Impact, the researchers are exploring how to bring the device to market and have filed a patent application covering the technology.

If future studies confirm the early results, this wearable ultrasound patch could become a valuable newly introduced tool for improving REM sleep and potentially addressing conditions associated with poor sleep.

Other members of the research team include William D. Moscoso-Barrera, Mengxia Yu, Mengmeng Yao, Jinmo Jeong, Ilya Pyatnitskiy, Anakaren Romero Lozano, Jiachen Wang, Ju-Chun Hsieh, Tony Sungjin Chae, Daniel Song, Julieta Garcia, Rithvik Mittapalli, and Adam Bush of the Department of Biomedical Engineering; Benjamin Baird of the College of Natural Sciences' Department of Psychology; and Wynn Legon of Virginia Tech's Fralin Biomedical Research Institute.

Materials provided by University of Texas at Austin. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

F1 and Manufacturers Unanimously Agree to a Proposal to Return to V8 Engines in 2030
